stories.headline: Anthropic Signs Deal for All of SpaceX's Colossus 1 Capacity, Doubles Claude Code Rate Limits

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, gaining access to more than 300 MW of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs including H100, H200, and GB200 accelerators) within the month.
key_facts.excerpt: We've signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at their Colossus 1 data center. This gives us access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) within the month.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, removed the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts, and raised API rate limits considerably for Claude Opus models — all effective May 6.
key_facts.excerpt: First, we're doubling Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. Second, we're removing the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts. Third, we're raising our API rate limits considerably for Claude Opus models.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity, as compute required for next-generation systems is outpacing terrestrial power, land, and cooling.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of this agreement, we have also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: The deal adds to Anthropic's existing compute portfolio: up to 5 GW agreement with Amazon (nearly 1 GW by end of 2026), 5 GW deal with Google and Broadcom (starting 2027), $30B Microsoft-NVIDIA Azure partnership, and $50B US AI infrastructure investment with Fluidstack.
key_facts.excerpt: An up to 5 gigawatt (GW) agreement with Amazon... a 5 GW agreement with Google and Broadcom... a strategic partnership with Microsoft and NVIDIA that includes $30 billion of Azure capacity... our $50 billion investment in American AI infrastructure with Fluidstack.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk reversed his stance on Anthropic after spending time with senior members last week, saying 'No one set off my evil detector' — having called Anthropic 'misanthropic and evil' as recently as February.
key_facts.excerpt: In February, he declared on X that 'Anthropic hates Western Civilization'... 'I spent a lot of time last week with senior members of the Anthropic team to understand what they do to ensure Claude is good for humanity and was impressed,' Musk tweeted. 'No one set off my evil detector.'

key_facts.fact: The deal gives IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee AI customer weeks before its planned public listing targeting a $1.75T–$2T valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and roadshow set for the week of June 8.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX filed confidentially with the SEC on April 1 for an IPO targeting a $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and the roadshow set for the week of June 8.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's surging demand has been driven partly by users moving away from OpenAI after military contract controversy, increasing adoption of Claude Code in professional software development, and a shift from single-agent chat to multi-agent workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: The increase has been driven partly by users moving away from OpenAI after controversy over its agreements with the United States military, increasing adoption of Claude Code in professional software development organizations, and a user behavior (and product) shift away from single-agent, chat-based tasks.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 'Dreaming' for Claude Managed Agents, Enabling Self-Improvement Between Sessions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched 'dreaming' as a research preview in Claude Managed Agents — a scheduled process that reviews past agent sessions and memory stores, extracts patterns, and curates memories so agents improve over time.
key_facts.excerpt: Dreaming is a scheduled process that reviews your agent sessions and memory stores, extracts patterns, and curates memories so your agents improve over time.

key_facts.fact: Dreaming surfaces patterns a single agent can't see, including recurring mistakes, workflows agents converge on, and team-wide preferences; users can choose automatic memory updates or review changes first.
key_facts.excerpt: Dreaming surfaces patterns that a single agent can't see on its own, including recurring mistakes, workflows that agents converge on, and preferences shared across a team. It also restructures memory so it stays high-signal as it evolves.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also made 'outcomes' generally available — a feature where a rubric-based grader evaluates agent output in a separate context window and the agent self-corrects, improving task success by up to 10 points over standard prompting.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing, outcomes improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems. Outcomes also improved file generation quality, with +8.4% task success on docx and +10.1% on pptx.

key_facts.fact: Multiagent orchestration was also made broadly available, allowing a lead agent to delegate subtasks to specialist agents with separate context windows and tools, while maintaining a shared memory store.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're... making outcomes, multiagent orchestration, and webhooks available to developers building with Managed Agents. Together, these updates make agents more capable at handling complex tasks with minimal steering.

key_facts.fact: The features were announced at Anthropic's Code with Claude developer conference in San Francisco, where CEO Dario Amodei said the company could grow by 80x in 2026 and its growth rate is 'too hard to handle.'
key_facts.excerpt: The announcements were made as Anthropic held a developer day in San Francisco where it touted a new feature for its Claude AI, which it calls 'dreaming.'

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Raises ~$2B at $20B+ Valuation Led by Meituan, ARR Tops $200M

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI, maker of the Kimi chatbot, raised approximately $2 billion in a new funding round at a post-money valuation above $20 billion, led by Meituan's Dragon Ball venture arm.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is on the verge of completing a new $2 billion funding round, a deal that will push the Kimi maker's valuation past $20 billion. The round is led by Meituan Dragonball.

key_facts.fact: Meituan Dragon Ball alone contributed over $200 million, with participation from China Mobile and CITIC Private Equity Funds (CPE).
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan Dragonball alone invested over $200 million, local media outlet LatePost reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot's valuation has more than quadrupled from ~$4.3 billion in November 2025 to over $20 billion; cumulative fundraising exceeds $3.9 billion in less than six months and $5.5 billion total.
key_facts.excerpt: In less than six months, Moonshot's valuation has more than quadrupled from about $4.3 billion last November. Including the latest injection, Moonshot has raised over $3.9 billion in the past half-year.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot's annual recurring revenue doubled from $100 million in early March to over $200 million in April 2026, driven by paid subscriptions and enterprise API calls.
key_facts.excerpt: Following the update of its K2.5 model, the company's annual recurring revenue (ARR) topped $100 million in early March. This revenue metric accelerated further in April, successfully breaching the $200 million mark.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot released and open-sourced its K2.6 model in April, which features enhanced coding capabilities and supports the collaboration of up to 300 sub-agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Ahead of the new funding, the company released and open-sourced its latest K2.6 model in April, which features enhanced coding capabilities and supports the collaboration of up to 300 sub-agents.

key_facts.fact: Founded by former Tsinghua University professor Yang Zhilin, Moonshot faces intense talent competition and plans to significantly boost employee stock option incentives this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Due to its outstanding performance in the coding domain, its core employees have become prime poaching targets for competitors. To cope with the intense industry rivalry, Moonshot plans to significantly boost employee stock option incentives this year.

stories.headline: Scale AI Wins $500M Pentagon Contract, Five Times Its Previous $100M Deal

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon awarded Scale AI a $500 million contract to help sift through data and assist in military decision-making, a five-fold increase from its $100 million deal signed in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Scale AI has won a $500m contract from the US Department of Defense, five times its previous deal... a five-fold expansion of the company's existing relationship with the department.

key_facts.fact: The contract was signed with the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), the principal procurement vehicle for US military AI integration spending.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement was signed with the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, the procurement vehicle driving the bulk of US military AI integration spending in 2025 and 2026.

key_facts.fact: Dan Tadross, who leads Scale AI's public sector business, said the Pentagon was 'pushing the limits' on the original contract and the deal shows the department is 'eager to adopt this technology.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon was 'pushing the limits' on the original contract, Dan Tadross, who leads Scale AI's public sector business, said in an interview. 'I think this contract is just generally proof that the department is eager to adopt this technology.'

key_facts.fact: Scale AI participates in the Defense Innovation Unit's Thunderforge programme and Trump's Golden Dome homeland defense framework, and its Scale Donovan platform deploys AI agents on networks classified up to Top Secret.
key_facts.excerpt: The company participates in the Defense Innovation Unit's Thunderforge programme... It contributes to Trump's Golden Dome homeland defense framework. Its Scale Donovan platform deploys mission-tailored AI agents on networks classified up to Top Secret.

key_facts.fact: Meta holds a 49% equity stake in Scale AI; the company developed Defense Llama, a national-security language model built on Meta's Llama 3 framework, for classified government deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's ownership stake, secured last year at 49 percent equity... Scale developed Defense Llama, a national-security language model built on top of Meta's Llama 3 framework.

stories.headline: Google Releases Multi-Token Prediction Drafters for Gemma 4, Up to 3x Faster Inference

key_facts.fact: Google released Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) drafters for its Gemma 4 open-weight models, using speculative decoding to deliver up to 3x faster inference without any degradation in output quality or reasoning logic.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says these experimental models leverage a form of speculative decoding to take a guess at future tokens, which can speed up generation compared to the way models generate tokens on their own.

key_facts.fact: MTP drafters are smaller auxiliary models that predict several tokens at once while the main model waits for data; the main model then verifies all suggestions in a single pass, eliminating idle GPU cycles caused by memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
key_facts.excerpt: While the main model waits for its data, a small auxiliary model uses the idle capacity to suggest several tokens at once. The main model then checks all those suggestions in a single pass—if they're correct, they get accepted at once.

key_facts.fact: The speedup works across smartphones, local computers, and cloud applications; MTP drafters are available under the open Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and Kaggle.
key_facts.excerpt: The speedup works on smartphones, local computers, and cloud applications. The drafters are available under the open Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and Kaggle.

key_facts.fact: Gemma 4, introduced in early April and built on the same technology as Google's Gemini AI, has already been downloaded over 60 million times.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's Gemma 4 open-weight model, introduced in early April, has already been downloaded over 60 million times.

key_facts.fact: Google is also working to optimize Gemma 4 models of different weights for specific hardware such as Apple Silicon and NVIDIA A100 accelerators.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says it is also working to optimize Gemma 4 models of different weights for specific hardware, such as the Apple Silicon or the popular Nvidia A100.

stories.headline: Roche Agrees to Acquire PathAI for Up to $1.05B to Transform AI-Driven Diagnostics

key_facts.fact: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche agreed to acquire US-based PathAI, which makes AI-powered digital pathology tools, for up to $1.05 billion — $750 million upfront with up to $300 million in milestone-based payments.
key_facts.excerpt: Roche announced today that it has entered into a definitive merger agreement to acquire PathAI, a US-based company in digital pathology and AI-powered technology for pathology laboratories and the biopharma industry.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition builds on a partnership established in 2021 and expanded in 2024 to include development of AI-enabled companion diagnostic algorithms; the deal is expected to close in H2 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: This acquisition builds on the successful partnership between Roche and PathAI, established in 2021 and scaled up in 2024 to include the development of AI-enabled companion diagnostic algorithms.

key_facts.fact: PathAI's AISight Image Management System software integrates advanced AI analysis and workflow capabilities for digital pathology labs, enabling automated processing of high-resolution tissue images.
key_facts.excerpt: PathAI's AISight IMS software interface is efficient and user-friendly, seamlessly integrating advanced analysis and workflow capabilities within the digital pathology laboratory.

key_facts.fact: Roche Diagnostics CEO Matt Sause said the deal will combine PathAI's digital pathology tools with Roche's oncology diagnosis platforms to improve precision cancer diagnosis and potentially better patient outcomes.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Digital pathology has the potential to improve precision diagnosis of cancer and enable physicians to offer better tailored treatment regimens,' said Matt Sause, CEO of Roche Diagnostics.

key_facts.fact: PathAI will become part of Roche's Diagnostics division; Roche intends to scale PathAI's solutions globally and strengthen its biopharma services for precision medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: Subject to the closing of the transaction, which is expected in the second half of the year, the acquired entity will become part of the Diagnostics division.

stories.headline: AI Insurance Startup Corgi Raises $160M Series B at $1.3B Valuation, Becomes YC's Latest Unicorn

key_facts.fact: Corgi, an AI-native full-stack insurance startup for startups, raised $160 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, led by TCV — becoming Y Combinator's latest unicorn.
key_facts.excerpt: Corgi announced today it has raised $160 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, advancing its mission to build the first AI-native, full-stack insurance platform for startups.

key_facts.fact: The round comes just four months after Corgi's $108 million across seed and Series A; total funding to date exceeds $268 million, with investors including YC, Kindred Ventures, and Contrary.
key_facts.excerpt: This comes just four months after the company announced a $108 million Series A. The company has now raised $268 million in funding to date.

key_facts.fact: Founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua in 2024 (YC Spring 2024 batch), Corgi uses AI systems to power underwriting, claims, and policy operations; customers include Deel and Artisan.
key_facts.excerpt: Laqua started the company with Emily Yuan in 2024 and was part of YC's Spring 2024 batch. Corgi, which names Deel and Artisan as customers, offers coverage for general liability, cyber liability, and tech and AI liability.

key_facts.fact: Corgi is expanding into new verticals beginning with trucking, and plans to move into payroll and small business insurance, automating workflows across the real economy.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is also moving into new verticals, beginning with trucking, where it plans to bring faster quoting, more adaptive risk models, and coverage aligned with real-world operations.

key_facts.fact: Corgi recently launched AI Insurance Coverage that integrates directly with existing tech E&O policies, offering modular coverage for AI-related risks including biased algorithms, harmful generated content, and autonomous system failures.
key_facts.excerpt: The coverage is built to address a wide spectrum of AI-related scenarios including issues stemming from biased algorithms, inaccurate or harmful generated content, misuse of training data, adversarial attacks on models.
